inputs:
Last Thursday morning, Daniel Mercer arrived at the office
earlier than usual. He had been working for several weeks
on a community project that connected local volunteers
with families who needed assistance. His longtime friend,
Rebecca Collins, could always be reached at
rebecca.collins@example.com. Daniel had originally
proposed building a small website to coordinate
volunteers, but as more people became interested, the
project quickly grew beyond its expectations. By the time
he finished his first cup of coffee, he had already
received messages from daniel.mercer@example.org,
volunteers@communityhub.test, and
sarah.johnson@example.net.

Around lunchtime, Daniel met with his colleague Marcus
Bennett at a small café near the town square. Marcus
suggested contacting several local businesses, including a
bakery managed by someone using
orders@sunrisebakery.example and a printing company whose
general mailbox was support@brightprint.example. Marcus
also recommended reaching out to Emily Parker, a retired
teacher who had volunteered at similar events for years.
Her email address, emily.parker@example.net, was already
in Daniel's contact list.

By Friday afternoon, the project was gaining momentum. A
local technology company offered to donate several
refurbished laptops, provided that Daniel could arrange
transportation. The company's representative, Olivia Chen,
sent the details from olivia.chen@techbridge.example,
explaining that the equipment would be available the
following Wednesday. Meanwhile, a local photographer named
James Wilson volunteered to document the event and
promised to deliver edited photographs within a week
through jwilson.photography@example.org.

On Saturday, everything came together. Volunteers checked
in at the front desk, where a sign-up sheet listed
team.leads@communityhub.test for questions, and
dispatch@greenwaytransport.example confirmed the delivery
schedule.

select c.id, c.name, c.email, count(o.id) as order_count, sum(o.total) as lifetime_value, max(o.placed_at) as last_order from customers c left join orders o on o.customer_id = c.id and o.status in ('paid', 'shipped', 'delivered') where c.created_at >= '2025-01-01' and c.region = 'us-west' group by c.id, c.name, c.email having sum(o.total) > 500 order by lifetime_value desc, last_order desc limit 25;
